decomposition_notes: Sizing-driven split. The requirements doc describes a decision-then-execute initiative whose full task count (measurement + decision + first-vertical-slice) would total 14 tasks, well past the ~10-task soft cap. Split at the natural decide-vs-execute seam: G1 owns measurement + the decision document; G2 owns the first vertical slice of whichever path the decision selects. CROSS-GOAL CLAIM ORDERING: Claim G1 first and let its final task (the decision document) land in main BEFORE claiming G2. G2's first task cannot be scoped without G1's recommendation — its acceptance criteria reference the path G1 selects. Within each goal, tasks use array-index dependencies for sibling sequencing.

goals.title: Measure the current test suite and produce a decision document
goals.why: Today the test-suite question is debated on vibes — no one has data on which tests are slow, how often they flake, or what the mock-to-integration ratio looks like per module. Decisions land badly when nobody has the numbers.
goals.what: Capture baseline measurements, build a pain inventory, evaluate three candidate paths (status-quo-tighten / convention-overhaul / parallel-replacement), recommend one, and define the first vertical slice for whichever path is chosen.
goals.description: Decision artifact, not implementation. The output is a committed Markdown decision document that names the recommended path and the first vertical slice. G2 picks up from there.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Baseline measurements committed to a fixture
Pain inventory captured with concrete examples
Three candidate paths evaluated against the same rubric
A single recommendation is named with rationale
The first vertical slice is specified well enough that G2 can start without re-derivation
pitfalls: Do not skip the measurement pass — the cap of the whole initiative is that decisions need data, not vibes
Do not predetermine the recommendation before the data is in

tasks.title: Capture slowest-20 tests baseline
tasks.description: Run `mix test --trace --slowest 20` (or the framework equivalent) and commit the output as a baseline fixture. Includes wall-clock per test, file path, and tag.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Output committed at fixtures/test-suite-baseline-slowest-20.txt
Re-running on the same suite produces equivalent results (within 5%)

manual_tests: Run `mix test --trace --slowest 20` twice on a quiescent machine and confirm the top-20 ordering is stable within 5% wall-clock
Diff the committed fixtures/test-suite-baseline-slowest-20.txt against a fresh run exactly as the verification step's `diff -q` does
edge_cases: Cold-compile time of the first run inflating a test's apparent duration — discard a warm-up run before capturing
Background load on the dev laptop skewing the ranking between runs
Tests tagged :skip or excluded by default never appearing in the trace
testing_strategy.coverage_target: N/A — baseline capture, not code under test

security_considerations: Measurement task — captures test names, file paths, and timings only; no auth, user input, or data-access surface
Do not commit any credentials or tokens a --trace run might echo from test setup logs into the baseline fixture
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use `mix test --trace --slowest 20` as the canonical command from the verification_steps
Redirect combined stdout+stderr to the fixture exactly as the verification diff expects (`> file 2>&1`)
Store the raw tool output verbatim — do not hand-edit the rankings
pitfalls: Don't run the trace under parallel CI load — noise makes the top-20 unreproducible
Don't strip the file-path/tag columns — later path evaluations need to tell a legitimate integration test from avoidable mock-heavy setup
Don't count the first cold run's compile time as test time

tasks.title: Capture mock-to-integration ratio per module
tasks.description: Walk test/ directory; per module, count tests using Mox/stubs vs tests using Repo.checkout/Bypass. Commit the table as a baseline fixture.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Table committed at fixtures/test-suite-baseline-mock-ratio.md
Includes one row per top-level module in test/

verification_steps.step_text: Spot-check 3 modules in the table against actual test files

manual_tests: Spot-check 3 modules in fixtures/test-suite-baseline-mock-ratio.md against the actual test files per the verification step
Grep each module's test dir for Mox/stub usage vs Repo.checkout/Bypass and confirm the tallied counts match
edge_cases: A test that uses BOTH a Mox stub and Repo.checkout — apply one documented tie-break rule uniformly
Support/helper files that define stubs but assert nothing — exclude from the count
Modules with zero tests still needing a row or an explicit omission note

security_considerations: Analysis task — walks test/ and tallies pattern usage; no runtime execution, auth, or user-input surface
Ensure the committed table contains no environment-specific secrets pasted from test setup
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Classify by concrete markers: Mox/`stub`/`expect` -> mock; `Repo.checkout`/`Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox`/`Bypass` -> integration
Emit one row per top-level module in test/ as the acceptance criteria requires
Record the classification rule at the top of the table so the ratio is reproducible
pitfalls: Don't conflate `async: true` with 'mock-based' — async DB tests use the sandbox, not mocks
Don't double-count a test that touches multiple boundaries; pick one rule and apply it uniformly
Don't leave the tie-break rule undocumented — the ratio is meaningless without it

tasks.title: Capture flake rate over the last 14 CI days
tasks.description: Scrape recent CI runs (or a representative log archive) and tally tests that flipped pass/fail without code changes. Commit per-test flake count.

verification_steps.step_text: Cross-reference CSV against a sample CI log

manual_tests: Cross-reference fixtures/test-suite-baseline-flakes-14d.csv against a sample CI log per the verification step
Recompute the aggregate flake-rate percentage from the per-test counts and confirm it matches the stated figure
edge_cases: CI history shorter than 14 days — state the actual window covered instead of silently truncating
Tests quarantined or marked flaky mid-window disappearing from later runs
A pass/fail flip caused by a real code change miscounted as a flake — only count flips with no intervening source change
A bimodal distribution where a few tests flake constantly and the rest never do

security_considerations: Reads CI run metadata and logs only; no auth or data-access surface in the app
CI logs can contain secrets/tokens — scrub any leaked values before committing the CSV or quoting log excerpts
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Count a flake only as a pass<->fail flip with no intervening source change on the same test
State the aggregate flake-rate percentage alongside the per-test CSV, as the acceptance criteria requires
Record the exact CI window (start/end dates, run count) so the rate is reproducible
pitfalls: Don't average away a bimodal distribution — report the shape, not just one mean percentage
Don't count skipped or quarantined tests as passing
Don't attribute a legitimate code-change failure to flakiness
Don't assume a full 14 days exists — note it if the archive is shorter

tasks.title: Build the pain inventory with concrete examples
tasks.description: Walk through 5-10 specific moments where the current architecture slowed a contributor down — with file paths, PR links, or commit refs as evidence.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
docs/decisions/test-suite-pain-inventory.md committed
Each item has at least one concrete reference (PR / commit / file)

verification_steps.step_text: Review committed file for concrete references

manual_tests: Review docs/decisions/test-suite-pain-inventory.md and confirm each of the 5-10 items carries at least one concrete PR/commit/file reference per the verification step
Follow two of the referenced PR/commit links and confirm they actually demonstrate the described slowdown
edge_cases: An anecdote with no traceable reference — find evidence or drop it rather than list a generic complaint
A pain point that is really about Wallaby/browser tests, which the requirements scope out
Duplicate anecdotes describing the same underlying root cause

security_considerations: Documentation task — no code or data-access surface
Do not paste internal credentials, private URLs, or contributor PII into the committed inventory when citing PRs/commits
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Every item cites at least one concrete PR link, commit ref, or file path — no generic complaints (acceptance criteria)
Ground each anecdote in the measurement fixtures where possible (slowest-20, mock ratio, flake CSV)
Keep browser/Wallaby pain out — the requirements scope it separately
pitfalls: Don't list vibes-based complaints without a traceable reference
Don't smuggle in Wallaby/browser-layer pain — it is explicitly out of scope
Don't inflate the count with duplicates of the same root cause

tasks.title: Evaluate path A: status quo + tighten slow tests
tasks.description: Score Path A against the measurement data. Estimate effort to bring the slowest-20 tests under target.

verification_steps.step_text: Review eval against the data fixtures

manual_tests: Review docs/decisions/test-suite-path-a.md against the four data fixtures (slowest-20, mock ratio, flake CSV, pain inventory) and confirm every claim is data-grounded per the verification step
Sanity-check the effort estimate for bringing the slowest-20 under target against the actual per-test timings
edge_cases: A slow test that is legitimately integration-bound and cannot be tightened without losing coverage (constraint: no coverage loss)
The measurement showing the 45s wall-clock is not broadly bottlenecking — Path A becomes the default per the open questions
An effort estimate dominated by a single outlier test

security_considerations: Analysis/decision task — reads committed measurement fixtures only; no auth, user-input, or data-access surface
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Score Path A against the SAME rubric used for B and C so the three evaluations are comparable (goal acceptance criteria)
Ground every claim in the committed data fixtures rather than intuition
Separate legitimately-slow integration tests from avoidable mock-heavy setup when estimating effort
pitfalls: Don't predetermine the outcome — let the slowest-20 and flake data drive the score
Don't propose deleting tests to hit the target; the constraint forbids coverage loss
Don't use a different rubric than paths B and C

tasks.title: Evaluate path B: convention overhaul without replacement
tasks.description: Score Path B (mandate Bypass for HTTP, Repo.checkout for DB, kill mox stubs) against the measurement data.

verification_steps.step_text: Review eval against the data fixtures

manual_tests: Review docs/decisions/test-suite-path-b.md against fixtures/test-suite-baseline-mock-ratio.md and confirm the convention-overhaul effort is grounded in the per-module counts
Confirm the eval uses the same rubric as paths A and C
edge_cases: Modules where killing Mox stubs would force a real external dependency with no Bypass seam
A staged rollout that can't be enforced without a lint/CI gate
Modules already following the target convention (zero migration cost) vs. the worst offenders

security_considerations: Analysis/decision task — reads committed measurement fixtures only; no auth or data-access surface
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Anchor the effort estimate in the per-module mock-vs-integration counts from fixtures/test-suite-baseline-mock-ratio.md
Score against the shared rubric used for A and C
Stage the convention change (Bypass for HTTP, Repo.checkout for DB) rather than a big-bang flag day, per the constraints
pitfalls: Don't assume every Mox stub has a clean Bypass/Repo.checkout replacement — flag the ones that don't
Don't propose a big-bang cutover; the constraints require incremental shippability
Don't diverge from the A/C rubric

tasks.title: Evaluate path C: parallel replacement under test_v2
tasks.description: Score Path C (start a parallel test architecture; migrate module by module) against the measurement data.

verification_steps.step_text: Review eval against the data fixtures

manual_tests: Review docs/decisions/test-suite-path-c.md against the data fixtures and confirm the module-by-module migration estimate is grounded
Confirm the eval respects the 'no permanent duplicate suite in CI' constraint and uses the shared rubric
edge_cases: The migration window overrunning and leaving two suites in CI permanently (constraint violation)
A module whose coverage cannot be re-asserted in the new layer without gaps (constraint: every replaced test needs an equivalent assertion)
test_v2/ and test/ both collected by `mix test`, doubling runtime during the window

security_considerations: Analysis/decision task — reads committed measurement fixtures only; no auth or data-access surface
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Score against the shared rubric used for A and B
Respect the constraints: no permanent dual-suite in CI, every replaced test keeps an equivalent assertion, `mix test`/`mix test --cover` entry points stay intact
Order the module-by-module migration using the mock-ratio fixture so the highest-pain modules go first
pitfalls: Don't propose a parallel suite that runs indefinitely — the constraint caps duplication to the migration window
Don't allow coverage to drop during migration — each moved test needs an equivalent assertion
Don't break the existing `mix test` entry point by adding test_v2/ to the default run without a plan

tasks.title: Write the recommendation and first-vertical-slice spec
tasks.description: Pick one of A/B/C with rationale; name the first vertical slice (specific module to migrate / specific tests to tighten / specific convention to mandate) that G2 will execute.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md committed
First vertical slice is specific enough that G2 can scope tasks without re-derivation

verification_steps.step_text: Confirm the recommendation names the first vertical slice precisely

manual_tests: Confirm docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md names exactly one of A/B/C with rationale and specifies the first vertical slice precisely per the verification step
Hand the first-slice spec to a fresh reader and confirm they can scope G2's tasks without re-deriving anything
edge_cases: The data supporting no change — the recommendation defaults to Path A per the open questions
A first slice too large to ship in one sprint (success metric requires roughly one sprint / ~30 tests)
Two paths scoring nearly equally — record the tie-break rationale

security_considerations: Decision-writing task — synthesizes committed fixtures and path evals; no code or data-access surface
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Follow the decision-document section order from the requirements Sketch: baseline -> pain -> three paths -> recommendation -> first slice
Name ONE path with a one-paragraph rationale (requirements Sketch section 4)
Specify the first vertical slice concretely enough that G2 scopes tasks without re-derivation (goal acceptance criteria)
pitfalls: Don't leave the first slice vague — G2 is blocked on it and cannot re-derive scope
Don't recommend a slice larger than one sprint / ~30 tests
Don't contradict the path evaluations; the recommendation must follow from the scored rubric

goals.title: Implement the first vertical slice from the test-suite decision
goals.why: The decision document from G1 names a specific first vertical slice. G2 ships it.
goals.what: Execute the first vertical slice as specified in docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md. The exact scope depends on the recommendation: tightening the slowest-20 (Path A), enforcing a convention on a representative module (Path B), or migrating one module under test_v2/ (Path C).
goals.where_context: test/ — exact paths depend on the recommendation
goals.description: BLOCKED on G1. The first task here cannot be scoped until docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md lands in main with the first-vertical-slice spec.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
First vertical slice as specified is implemented
Before/after measurements show the expected delta (faster, fewer mocks, etc.)
No regression in pass rate of the existing suite
Documentation updated to reflect the new convention or layer
pitfalls: Do not deviate from the recommendation's first-slice scope — broader changes belong in follow-up tasks
Do not break the existing `mix test` and `mix test --cover` entry points

tasks.title: Re-read the recommendation and confirm the first-vertical-slice scope
tasks.description: Open docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md, identify the named first slice, and confirm the scope is still applicable (no relevant test changes since G1 landed).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Notes added to the recommendation doc confirming the slice scope or flagging the need for a recommendation refresh

verification_steps.step_text: Read the slice description against current test/ contents

manual_tests: Read the first-slice description in docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md against current test/ contents and confirm the scope is still applicable per the verification step
Check git log on the targeted test files since G1 landed for changes that would invalidate the slice
edge_cases: Test files in the slice's scope changed since G1 landed — flag for a recommendation refresh rather than proceeding
The named module having been split or renamed since the decision
The recommendation defaulting to Path A (tighten in place) with no distinct module to confirm

security_considerations: Read/annotation task — reads the decision doc and test/ tree; no auth or data-access surface
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Add a dated slice-confirmation note to the recommendation doc rather than editing the original decision prose
Compare the slice scope against current test/ state, not the state at G1 authoring time
Flag-and-stop if scope drifted rather than silently re-scoping
pitfalls: Don't start implementation before confirming the slice still applies
Don't silently rewrite the recommendation's scope — flag a refresh if test/ drifted
Don't overwrite the original decision rationale; append a confirmation note

tasks.title: Implement the first slice — primary code change
tasks.description: Make the changes called for by the first vertical slice. Exact files depend on the recommendation; the test description there is your scope.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Code change as specified is in place
Unit tests pass after the change

unit_tests: Run the affected module's tests with `mix test <slice test path>` and confirm they pass after the change
For any test moved off a Mox stub onto Repo.checkout/Bypass, add an equivalent behavioural assertion so coverage does not drop (constraint: no coverage loss)
integration_tests: If the slice replaces a mock boundary with a real one, exercise the module end-to-end through the new Bypass/Repo.checkout seam
manual_tests: Run the full `mix test` per the verification step and confirm no unrelated breakage
edge_cases: A test that asserted on mock interaction (verify/expect) with no behavioural equivalent in the new layer
async: true tests colliding under the new DB-state strategy
Shared setup helpers used by both migrated and un-migrated tests
testing_strategy.coverage_target: No decrease versus the G1 baseline for the affected module

security_considerations: Test-infrastructure change — modifies test setup/assertions, not production code paths; low security surface
If the slice introduces Bypass/HTTP seams, ensure no real credentials or live endpoints are hardcoded into the test setup
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
The first-slice description in docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md is the scope of record — implement exactly it
Match the target convention the recommendation mandates (e.g. Bypass for HTTP, Repo.checkout for DB)
Keep the existing `mix test` entry point green throughout (constraint)
pitfalls: Don't broaden beyond the first slice — follow-ups belong in a later task
Don't drop a mock-interaction assertion without an equivalent behavioural assertion (constraint: no coverage loss)
Don't break `mix test`/`mix test --cover` — they're wired into hooks and scripts

tasks.title: Capture before/after measurement against the slice's target metric
tasks.description: Run the same measurement procedure G1 ran for the affected module; commit the after-figure.

verification_steps.step_text: Confirm before/after delta matches the recommendation's predicted delta

manual_tests: Re-run the same measurement procedure G1 used for the affected module (e.g. `mix test --trace` on the slice's tests) and record the after-figure
Confirm fixtures/test-suite-slice-after.md contains a before/after table and the delta matches or beats the recommendation's prediction per the verification step
edge_cases: Warm-vs-cold run skew — reuse the exact warm-up protocol G1 used so before/after stay comparable
A delta within measurement noise — state the noise band rather than claiming a win
The 'before' figure needing to come from the G1 baseline fixture, not a fresh re-run of old code

security_considerations: Measurement task — records timings/counts only; no auth or data-access surface
Do not let --trace setup logs leak secrets into the committed after-fixture
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use the IDENTICAL measurement procedure and warm-up protocol from G1 so before/after are apples-to-apples
Pull the 'before' number from the committed G1 baseline fixture rather than re-deriving it
Commit a before/after table to fixtures/test-suite-slice-after.md (acceptance criteria)
pitfalls: Don't compare a cold 'after' run against a warm 'before' baseline
Don't claim a delta inside the noise band as a real improvement
Don't invent a 'before' number — cite the G1 baseline fixture

tasks.title: Confirm no regression in pass rate on the existing suite
tasks.description: Run `mix test --cover` end-to-end; verify pass rate and coverage match baseline.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
mix test --cover passes
Coverage unchanged or improved relative to baseline

verification_steps.expected_result: All tests pass; coverage at/above baseline

integration_tests: Run `mix test --cover` end-to-end per the verification step and confirm all tests pass
manual_tests: Compare the reported pass count and coverage percentage against the G1 baseline and confirm unchanged-or-improved per the acceptance criteria
edge_cases: The coverage tool counting new/migrated tests differently, shifting the percentage without a real regression
A newly-flaky test surfacing intermittently — re-run to distinguish flake from regression
async ordering exposing a latent inter-test dependency introduced by the slice
testing_strategy.coverage_target: At or above the G1 baseline coverage percentage

security_considerations: Verification task — runs the existing suite; no auth or data-access surface
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use `mix test --cover` — the entry point the constraints require to stay intact
Compare against the committed G1 baseline, not a remembered number
Re-run once before declaring a regression to rule out a flake (see the flake baseline)
pitfalls: Don't accept a coverage drop as 'close enough' — the acceptance criteria require at/above baseline
Don't mistake a known flaky test for a slice-caused regression
Don't skip the full-suite run by only testing the changed module

tasks.title: Update CONTRIBUTING / AGENTS notes to reflect the new convention
tasks.description: Adjust the project's contributor docs so the next contributor knows about the new pattern or layering established by the slice.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md updated
The new convention is named explicitly

manual_tests: Re-read the updated AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md section and confirm it names the new convention explicitly and clearly per the verification step
Confirm the section states which layer/boundary the pattern governs so the next contributor can apply it unprompted
edge_cases: The convention only applying to the migrated module so far — word the doc so it does not imply project-wide adoption
Conflicting existing testing guidance in AGENTS.md that must be reconciled, not duplicated

security_considerations: Documentation edit — no code or data-access surface
Do not commit tokens, internal URLs, or credentials into the contributor docs when giving examples
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Name the new convention explicitly (acceptance criteria) and state which boundary it governs (HTTP -> Bypass, DB -> Repo.checkout, etc.)
Match the existing AGENTS.md tone and section structure rather than bolting on a new format
Scope the wording to what the first slice actually established — mark the rest as forthcoming
pitfalls: Don't overstate rollout — the convention currently covers one slice, not the whole suite
Don't duplicate or contradict existing testing guidance already in AGENTS.md
Don't paste secrets into example snippets

tasks.title: Define follow-up slices and update the recommendation doc
tasks.description: Based on what worked and what surprised in the first slice, define the next 2-3 vertical slices in the recommendation doc.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md gets a 'Follow-up slices' section
Each next-slice item is specific enough to become a Stride task

verification_steps.step_text: Confirm each next slice can be scoped without further discussion

manual_tests: Confirm docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md gains a 'Follow-up slices' section and each next-slice item is specific enough to become a Stride task per the verification step
Hand each next-slice bullet to a fresh reader and confirm it can be scoped without further discussion
edge_cases: A first-slice surprise invalidating the assumed migration order — reorder rather than follow the stale plan
A follow-up slice that is really several slices — split it so each fits one sprint / ~30 tests
The first slice revealing the whole path was wrong — flag a recommendation revisit instead of listing follow-ups

security_considerations: Planning/documentation task — appends to the decision doc; no code or data-access surface
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Ground the next 2-3 slices in what actually worked and surprised in the first slice (task description)
Size each follow-up like the first slice: one sprint, ~30 tests, single module/boundary
Write each item concretely enough to become a Stride task without re-derivation (acceptance criteria)
pitfalls: Don't list vague 'migrate everything else' items — each slice must be independently scopable
Don't ignore first-slice surprises when ordering follow-ups
Don't bundle multiple modules into one oversized slice
